title: PR validator/reviewer loop with human final approval gate
body:
Part of: #165
Depends on: #239, #241
Related workflows: `.github/workflows/qa-publish.yml`, `.github/workflows/codex-headless-pr.yml`

## Summary
Agent-created PRs need a consistent validator/reviewer loop before they are treated as fixed, merged, or promoted.

We already have the underlying validation and proof-publish pieces, but not a dedicated PR-triggered control-plane issue that ties them together with explicit human final approval.

## Red
- PRs created by agents are not yet guaranteed to run a consistent `validate -> verify-fix -> publish proof -> review summary` loop.
- Human final approval for merge/production is described, but not tracked as a first-class delivery issue.
- There is no clear retry cap/escalation rule when machine or human review blocks a PR.

## Green
Every agent-created PR gets validation, reviewer-visible proof, structured machine review output, and an explicit human final approval gate before merge or production promotion.

## Scope
- Add a PR-triggered validator workflow for agent-created PRs
- Re-run the relevant validation/`--verify-fix` path using issue/finding metadata
- Publish reviewer-visible evidence using the trusted QA publish flow when applicable
- Leave a structured PR summary with:
  - verdict
  - confidence
  - unresolved risks
  - proof links
- Optionally run a second-model review pass, or document the fallback if human-only review remains the gate
- Define retry/escalation policy:
  - max automated rework cycles
  - when to stop and route to a human
- Keep merge/prod approval human-gated even when validator passes

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Agent-created PRs automatically run validation and attach or link reviewer-visible evidence
- [ ] The PR gets a structured validator/reviewer summary with verdict and confidence
- [ ] Blocking machine or human feedback can requeue implementation only within an explicit retry cap
- [ ] Ambiguous/non-portable PRs are routed to a human instead of looping indefinitely
- [ ] Merge to `main` and promotion to production still require explicit human approval
- [ ] The final approval boundary is documented in repo-visible workflow/docs, not just implied by convention

## Suggested Lane
`qa-platform` with `infra-deploy` review

## Suggested Execution Mode
`safe-unattended` for validation; human approval required for merge and production promotion
